extracted.intended_audience: participants, petitioners, licensees, and counsel in NRC adjudicatory proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory rules (10 CFR Part 2) governing service, computation of time, requests for hearings and petitions to intervene, standing, contention admissibility, selection of hearing procedures, interlocutory review, presiding officer designation, appearance and conduct, and sanctions in NRC adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on the NRC staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Service shall be made upon the NRC staff of all documents required to be filed with participants and the presiding officer in all proceedings, including those proceedings where the NRC staff informs the presiding officer of its determination not to participate as a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service upon the NRC staff shall be by the same or equivalent method as service upon the Office of the Secretary and the presiding officer (e.g., electronically, personal delivery or courier, express mail, or expedited delivery service). If no attorney representing the NRC Staff has filed a notice of appearance and service is not via E-Filing, specified delivery addresses/modes (Deputy General Counsel delivery, mail, email to RidsOgcMailCenter.Resource@nrc.gov, or facsimile to 301-415-3200) must be used. If staff decides not to participate as a party it shall designate a person and address for service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: In computing any period of time, the day of the act, event, or default after which the designated period begins to run is not included; the last day is included unless it falls on a Saturday, Sunday, Federal legal holiday at the place the action is to occur, or a day of emergency Federal closure of NRC Headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the last day is excluded by the above, the period runs until the end of the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, Federal legal holiday, or emergency closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time — additional days for service method
rubrics_metrics.description: When a participant must act within a prescribed period after service of a notice/document, additional days are added depending on the method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If served by first-class mail only, add 3 calendar days for all participants; if served by express mail or other expedited service only, add 2 calendar days. If served by multiple methods, compute additional days according to the service method used to deliver the entire document (excluding courtesy copies); the presiding officer may determine calculation when entitlement to receive the entire filing varies. In mixed-service proceedings where participants use different methods, the presiding officer will determine number of days based on fairness and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — time-of-day filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered timely, a document must be served by specified times of day depending on the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By 5 p.m. Eastern Time for a document served in person or by expedited service; by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time for a document served by the E-Filing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and reduction of time limits; delegated authority for SUNSI access procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided by law, prescribed time periods may be extended or shortened by the Commission or the presiding officer for good cause, or by stipulation approved by them; if no time limit is prescribed, the Commission or presiding officer may set one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary is delegated authority to issue orders establishing procedures and timelines for submitting and resolving requests for access to safeguards information or sensitive unclassified non-safeguards information where necessary to meet intervention requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of requests for hearing by the Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a request for hearing or petition to intervene, the Secretary will forward the request/petition and proffered contentions and any answers/replies either to the Commission for a ruling or to the Chief Administrative Judge of the Atomic Safety and Licensing Board Panel for designation of a presiding officer under § 2.313(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: General requirement to file request for hearing and contentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person whose interest may be affected and who desires to participate as a party must file a written request for hearing and a specification of the contentions to be litigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In proceedings under § 52.103 or § 53.1452 the Commission (acting as presiding officer) will grant the request only if the requester has standing (see paragraph (d)) and has proposed at least one admissible contention meeting paragraph (f). For other proceedings, the Commission/presiding officer/ASLB will grant the request if standing and at least one admissible contention are met; applicant/licensee is deemed a party when filing in response to a notice of hearing or opportunity for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — filing deadlines for hearing requests/petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for filing requests/petitions and contentions depend on the proceeding type and notice publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer of control proceedings: 20 days from Federal Register notice publication. High-level radioactive waste geologic repository initial authorization: 30 days from Federal Register notice. Proceedings with Federal Register notice (other than above): time specified in notice or not less than 60 days from notice; if no period specified, 60 days from publication. Proceedings without Federal Register notice: latest of (i) 60 days after publication on NRC major actions web page, or (ii) 60 days after actual notice but not more than 60 days after agency action on application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filings after the deadline — good cause for late filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing requests, intervention petitions, and motions for leave to file new or amended contentions filed after the deadline will not be entertained absent a presiding officer determination that the participant has demonstrated good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good cause requires showing that (i) the information upon which the filing is based was not previously available; (ii) the information is materially different from information previously available; and (iii) the filing was submitted in a timely fashion based on availability of the subsequent information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of §§ 2.307 and 2.323 to late filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing changes to deadlines and other procedural statutes interact with late filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 2.307 applies to requests to change a filing deadline (requested before or after that deadline has passed) based on reasons not related to the substance of the filing. § 2.323 does not apply to hearing requests, intervention petitions, or motions for leave to file new or amended contentions filed after the deadline in paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: New petitioner late filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing request or intervention petition filed after the deadline by a new petitioner must include contentions and must demonstrate that the petitioner meets applicable standing and contention admissibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party/participant new or amended contentions after deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A new or amended contention filed by a party or participant after the deadline must meet applicable contention admissibility requirements in paragraph (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the party/participant has already satisfied standing requirements in the same proceeding, it does not need to re-demonstrate standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing — required contents of a request/petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for hearing or petition for leave to intervene must state: (i) the name, address and telephone number of the requestor/petitioner; (ii) the nature of the requestor's/petitioner's right under the Act to be made a party; (iii) the nature and extent of the requestor's/petitioner's property, financial or other interest in the proceeding; and (iv) the possible effect of any decision or order on the requestor's/petitioner's interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulings on standing
rubrics_metrics.description: In ruling on a request for hearing or petition to intervene, the Commission/presiding officer/ASLB must determine, among other things, whether the petitioner has an interest affected by the proceeding considering the factors enumerated in paragraph (d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing in enforcement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In enforcement proceedings, the licensee or other person against whom the action is taken shall have standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary intervention — factors to address
rubrics_metrics.description: When at least one petitioner has standing and at least one admissible contention has been admitted, the presiding officer may consider requests for discretionary intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner seeking discretionary intervention (in the event that standing as of right is not demonstrated) must address factors that will be considered and balanced: factors weighing in favor (i) extent to which participation may assist in developing a sound record; (ii) nature and extent of petitioner's interest; (iii) possible effect of decision on petitioner's interest; and factors weighing against (i) availability of other means to protect interest; (ii) extent interest will be represented by existing parties; (iii) extent participation will inappropriately broaden issues or delay proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentions — specificity and particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for hearing or petition for leave to intervene must set forth with particularity the contentions sought to be raised. For each contention the petition must meet multiple subrequirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each contention must: (i) provide a specific statement of the issue of law or fact to be raised or controverted (Part 52/53 requests must be directed to acceptance criteria in combined license and operational consequences); (ii) provide a brief explanation of the basis for the contention; (iii) demonstrate the issue is within the scope of the proceeding; (iv) demonstrate the issue is material to findings the NRC must make; (v) provide a concise statement of alleged facts or expert opinions supporting the position with references to specific sources/documents; (vi) in non-Part52 proceedings provide sufficient information to show a genuine dispute with applicant/licensee, including references to specific portions of the application and supporting reasons, or identify deficiencies if required information is missing and explain why deficiency prevents prima facie showing; (vii) in Part52/53 proceedings include supporting information showing prima facie that acceptance criteria have not been met and the operational consequences would be contrary to reasonable assurance of adequate protection, including the specific portion of the report believed inaccurate/incomplete and explanation why it prevents the prima facie showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentions must be based on available documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Contentions must be based on documents or other information available at the time the petition is filed (e.g., application, supporting safety analysis report, environmental report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On NEPA issues, participants shall file contentions based on the applicant's environmental report. Participants may file new/amended environmental contentions after the deadline (e.g., based on draft/final NRC environmental impact statement, environmental assessment, or supplements) if the contention complies with late-filing requirements in paragraph (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-sponsored contentions and adoption of another's contention
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more requestors/petitioners seek to co-sponsor a contention, they shall jointly designate a representative with authority to act for them with respect to that contention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a requestor/petitioner seeks to adopt another sponsoring requestor/petitioner's contention, the adopting party must either agree that the sponsoring party will act as representative for that contention or jointly designate a representative who has authority to act for the requestors/petitioners with respect to that contention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of hearing procedures — controlling criteria and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determination that a request/petition should be granted and a hearing held, the Commission, presiding officer, or ASLB will determine and identify the specific hearing procedures to be used, with rules depending on subject matter and case-specific findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: proceedings for grant/renewal/amendment/termination of licenses or permits subject to listed parts may be conducted under subpart L except as provided. Enforcement matters: subpart G unless parties jointly request subpart L or N. Uranium enrichment licensing: subpart G. Nuclear power reactor matters where resolution necessitates resolving material fact issues about past activity, eyewitness credibility, or motive/intent: subpart G. Spent nuclear fuel storage expansion: subpart L unless party requests subpart K or all parties agree to subpart N. HLW geologic repository initial construction/licensing: subparts G and J; subsequent amendments may be under subpart L unless all parties agree to subpart N. Transfer of control requiring prior NRC approval: subpart M unless Commission orders otherwise. Proceedings otherwise eligible may be conducted under subpart N if hearing expected to take no more than two (2) days or all parties agree. Design certification informal hearings under part 52/53 must be under subpart O. Commission findings under § 52.103 and § 53.1452 conducted under procedures designated by the Commission. The Commission may conduct hearings under subpart O when it grants petitions under § 2.335(b) to assist in developing a record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory review — appealable orders and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: An order of the presiding officer (or Chief Administrative Judge or other designated administrative judge) may be appealed to the Commission with respect to requests for hearing, petitions to intervene, or requests for access to SUNSI/SGI; an officer designated to rule on information access issues may also be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be made within 25 days after service of the order by filing a notice of appeal and supporting brief; opposing parties may file a brief in opposition within 25 days after service of the appeal. Supporting brief and any answer must conform to § 2.341(c)(3). No other appeals from rulings on requests for hearing are allowed. An order denying a petition/request for access is appealable by the requester on whether it should have been granted. An order granting may be appealed by a party other than the requester on whether it should have been wholly denied; appeals re SGI may only be taken by NRC staff; appeals re SUNSI only by NRC staff or a party whose independent interest would be harmed. An order selecting a hearing procedure may be appealed by any party on whether the selection was in clear contravention of criteria set forth in § 2.310; such appeal must be filed no later than ten (10) days after issuance of the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When terms of a notice of hearing are not otherwise prescribed, the order/notice of hearing must state: (1) the nature of the hearing and its time and place (or that time/place will be fixed later); (2) the legal authority and jurisdiction; (3) the matters of fact and law asserted or to be considered; and (4) a statement describing the specific hearing procedures or subpart to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time and place of hearing will be fixed with due regard for convenience of parties/representatives, nature of proceeding, and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of presiding officer — default appointment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may provide in the notice of hearing that particular officials (Commission members, ALJ, administrative judge, ASLB, or a named delegated officer) shall be the presiding officer. The Commission alone designates the presiding officer in hearings under subpart O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission does not designate the presiding officer for hearings under subparts G, J, K, L, M, or N, the Chief Administrative Judge shall issue an order designating (1) an Atomic Safety and Licensing Board or an administrative law judge for hearings under subparts G, J, K, L, or N; or (2) an ASLB, an administrative law judge, or an administrative judge for hearings under subpart M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: If a designated presiding officer or ASLB member believes they are disqualified to preside or participate, they shall withdraw by notice on the record and notify the Commission or Chief Administrative Judge of the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party believes a presiding officer or ASLB member should be disqualified, the party may move that the presiding officer/board member disqualify themselves. The motion must be supported by affidavits setting forth alleged grounds; if the presiding officer does not grant the motion or the member does not disqualify, the motion must be referred to the Commission which will determine sufficiency of grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavailability and substitution of presiding officer/board member
rubrics_metrics.description: If a presiding officer or ASLB member becomes unavailable during a hearing, the Commission or Chief Administrative Judge will designate another presiding officer or board member. If they become unavailable after the hearing has concluded, the Commission may designate another presiding officer, the Chief Administrative Judge or Commission may designate another ASLB member to participate in the decision, or the Commission may direct that the record be certified to it for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a presiding officer or ASLB member is substituted for the originally designated one, any motion predicated upon the substitution must be made within five (5) days after the substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of practice and decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: In exercising their functions under this subpart, the Commission, ASLBs, ALJs, and Administrative Judges function in a quasi-judicial capacity; parties and their representatives are expected to conduct themselves with honor, dignity, and decorum as they should before a court of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation — who may appear and notice of appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may appear on their own behalf or by an attorney-at-law. Partnerships, corporations, or unincorporated associations may be represented by a duly authorized member or officer, or by an attorney-at-law. Attorneys must be in good standing and admitted to practice before a U.S. Court, D.C., or the highest court of any State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person appearing in a representative capacity shall file a written notice of appearance stating name, address, telephone, facsimile and email (if any); the name and address of the person/entity represented; and, for attorneys, the basis of eligibility to represent, or for other representatives, the basis of authority to act on behalf of the party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprimand, censure, or suspension from participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer or the Commission may reprimand, censure, or suspend from participation in a particular proceeding any party or representative who refuses to comply with directions, or who is disorderly, disruptive, or engages in contemptuous conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reprimand, censure, or suspension ordered to run one day or less must state the grounds in the record and advise the disciplined person of the right to appeal. A suspension ordered for longer than one day must be in writing, state the grounds, and advise the person of the right to appeal and to request a stay. The suspension may be stayed for a reasonable time to allow the affected party to obtain other representation if necessary to prevent injustice. Anyone disciplined may file an appeal with the Commission within 25 days after issuance of the order; the appeal must be in writing and state concisely with supporting argument why the order was erroneous. The Commission will consider each appeal on the merits.
